title: Deep Global-sense Hard-negative Discriminative Generation Hashing for Cross-modal Retrieval
claim: Interpolating from isolated pairs ignores overall embedding geometry; interpolating with global correlation awareness keeps synthesized samples consistent with the distribution.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, left-to-right, dashed class boundaries with shared legend inset
description: Two side-by-side panels with rounded dashed borders compare 'Partial-sense Interpolation' (left) and 'Global-sense Interpolation' (right). Each shows the same 2-D embedding space: scattered green circles, blue triangles, red pentagons, purple diamonds and orange squares. Dark shapes are images and pale shapes are text. Teal dashed curves mark class regions. Circled anchor points connect by black arrows to red or blue pseudo-sample stars. On the left, the stars land in hatched pink and blue patches, some inside other classes' regions, so the generated points break the distribution. On the right, extra teal arrows run from neighboring samples to each star, and the stars sit consistently within the class structure. A legend box at the bottom center explains the symbols and arrow types. The eye goes first to the two italic titles, then to the arrows.
caption: Traditional generation methods only interpolate based on the correlation between single anchor-negative pairs, which damages the global distribution relationship of heterogeneous samples in the embedding co-space. Through the interpolation of hard negative samples with global awareness of sample correlation, the generated samples are controlled to avoid violating the feature distribution in the embedding space, which makes the co-space more discriminative.
abstract: Hard negative generation (HNG) provides valuable signals for deep learning, but existing methods mostly rely on local correlations while neglecting the global geometry of the embedding space. This limitation often leads to weak discrimination, particularly in cross-modal hashing, which obtains compact binary codes. We propose Deep Global-sense Hard-negative Discriminative Generation Hashing (DGHDGH), a framework that constructs a structured graph with dual-iterative message propagation to capture global correlations, and then performs difficulty-adaptive, channel-wise interpolation to synthesize semantically consistent hard negatives aligned with global Hamming geometry. Our approach yields more informative negatives, sharpens semantic boundaries in the Hamming co-space, and substantially enhances cross-modal retrieval. Experiments on multiple benchmarks consistently demonstrate improvements in retrieval accuracy, verifying the discriminative advantages brought by global-sense HNG in cross-modal hashing.
